title: In defence of the Ehrenfest mean-field molecular dynamics
abstract: Re-visiting the problem of the coupled electronic--nuclear motion, we prove that the so called `mean-field' Ehrenfest picture is an exact theory, rather than an approximation, in the classical limit for nuclei. By establishing its full equivalence to the much more involved Exact Factorization approach to the problem (Abedi {\it et al.}, Europhys. Lett. {\bf 106}, 33001 (2014)), our conclusion rehabilitates the mean-field Ehrenfest molecular dynamics as a simple, effective, while formally exact scheme, amenable to the use within the framework of the time-dependent density functional theory.
summary: This paper mathematically proves that the mean-field Ehrenfest approach for coupled electron-nuclear dynamics is an exact theory when nuclei are treated classically. By demonstrating its equivalence to the rigorous Exact Factorization method, the authors validate the use of this simple, effective scheme within Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT). This provides a strong theoretical foundation for simulating complex molecular systems.
main_problem: To rigorously prove that the mean-field Ehrenfest picture for coupled electronic-nuclear motion is an exact theory, rather than an approximation, in the classical limit for the nuclei.
main_result: The mean-field Ehrenfest molecular dynamics is proven to be mathematically equivalent to the more complex Exact Factorization approach in the classical limit, validating its use in TDDFT.
method: The authors use rigorous mathematical derivations, comparing the force derived from the full quantum evolution in the classical limit against the established results from the Exact Factorization formalism.
model_or_system: The system involves coupled electronic motion (governed by TDSE) and nuclear motion (treated classically), described by a mixed quantum-classical Hamiltonian.
key_observables: The force acting on the nuclei, $F_i(t)$, and the electronic density, $n_e(\mathbf{r}, t)$.
important_parameters: The strict classical limit for the heavy nuclei particles.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the mixed quantum-classical dynamics and the strict classical limit for the nuclei.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem, derives the force equation from the full quantum evolution, proves its equivalence to the Exact Factorization result through detailed mathematical steps (including appendices), and concludes by justifying the use of TDDFT.
why_interesting: This work provides a formal, exact justification for a widely used, computationally tractable method (Ehrenfest dynamics) in simulating molecular and condensed matter systems, which is crucial for theoretical work in open quantum systems and molecular dynamics.
